summary:
CROP ROTATION PREDICTION SYSTEM
Field Shift is a web-based agricultural decision-support system designed to help farmers select suitable crops and plan crop rotation using soil properties, previous crop history, farm location, water availability and climatic conditions. The system collects farm details, GPS coordinates, farm photographs, soil test results (pH, NPK), fertilizer information and previous crop sowing and harvesting dates. It integrates historical climate data retrieved through NASA POWER API based on farm GPS coordinates to assess local climatic conditions, including temperature and rainfall. Field Shift provides seven key functionalities: GPS-based farm identification, soil nutrient analysis, crop history recording, climate analysis, fertilizer information management, crop recommendation and crop rotation planning. These features help farmers identify suitable crops and alternative crops based on available agricultural information. The platform combines soil laboratory results, geographical location, historical climate data and previous crop information to support informed agricultural decisions. Its recommendation process uses implemented decision-making rules. Technologies Used: Python, Stream lit, NASA POWER API, GPS Coordinates, Soil Test Reports and GitHub. Intended Impact: Field Shift promotes sustainable farming, crop diversity, improved soil nutrient management, efficient agricultural resource utilization and climate-aware crop planning.
details:
PROJECT TITLE: FIELDSHIFT – CLIMATE-AWARE CROP RECOMMENDATION AND CROP ROTATION SYSTEM

Project Overview :

Field Shift is a web-based agricultural decision-support prototype designed to help farmers identify suitable crops and plan crop rotation based on farm details, soil properties, previous crop information and climatic conditions. The system uses NASA POWER climate data and soil-test information to support better agricultural planning and sustainable farming practices.

How It Works: The website collects essential information about the agricultural land through three main sections:

1. Farm Details
  • Assessment date of the agricultural land.
  • Uploading the original farm photograph.
  • Entering GPS coordinates (latitude and longitude).
  • Selecting the soil type.
  • Providing water availability details.
  • Entering the previously cultivated crop.
  • Recording previous crop sowing and harvesting dates.
2. Soil Test and Fertilizer Details
  • Entering soil pH values.
  • Providing Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P) and Potassium (K) values.
  • Selecting the units used in the soil-test report.
  • Entering fertilizers used and their grades or quantities.
3. NASA POWER Climate Data
  • Retrieving historical climate information using NASA POWER.
  • Selecting the historical period for climate analysis.
  • Analyzing the farm location using geographical coordinates.
  • Using climatic information to support crop suitability and crop rotation recommendations.
Benefits for former
  • Suitable Crop Selection: Recommends suitable crops based on soil properties, nutrients and climatic conditions.
  • Improved Crop Rotation: Helps farmers select the next crop based on previously cultivated crops.
  • Soil Health Management: Helps maintain soil fertility through soil-test-based crop and nutrient planning.
  • Water Conservation: Supports better irrigation planning using historical climate data.
  • Reduced Farming Costs: Helps minimize unnecessary fertilizer use and unsuitable crop cultivation.
  • Climate-Based Farming: Uses NASA POWER data to understand historical rainfall and temperature patterns.
  • Sustainable Agriculture: Promotes better utilization of natural resources and environmentally friendly farming practices.
Key Features
  • GPS-Based Farm Identification: Uses latitude and longitude to identify the agricultural land location.
  • Soil Analysis: Collects soil pH and NPK nutrient information.
  • Crop History: Considers previously cultivated crops and their sowing and harvesting dates.
  • Climate Analysis: Uses historical NASA POWER climate data.
  • Fertilizer Information: Records fertilizer types, grades and quantities.
  • Crop Recommendation: Supports the identification of suitable crops based on available farm information.
  • Crop Rotation Planning: Helps farmers consider alternative crops after previous cultivation.

Intended Impact

  • Encourages sustainable agricultural practices.
  • Supports better utilization of soil nutrients.
  • Helps farmers make informed crop-selection decisions.
  • Promotes climate-aware farming.
  • Supports improved agricultural planning and resource management.

Technology and Tools Used

  • Python – Application development and data processing.
  • Stream lit – Web application development and user interface.
  • NASA POWER API – Historical climate data retrieval.
  • GPS Coordinates – Geographical identification of farmland.
  • Soil Test Reports – Soil pH and nutrient information.
  • GitHub – Source-code storage and project management.
Our project aims to help farmers make better farming decisions using NASA satellite data and soil information. It helps identify suitable crops, improve soil health, follow proper crop rotation, and reduce unnecessary fertilizer usage. It also supports sustainable farming by providing useful recommendations based on soil and environmental conditions. Our main goal is to increase agricultural productivity, protect soil fertility, and promote smarter farming for a better future.Development Tools and Technology Stack:
  • Programming Language: Python – Used for data processing, calculations, soil analysis, and implementing the project's core logic.
  • Development Environment: Visual Studio Code – Used for writing, editing, debugging, and managing Python code.
  • Version Control & Repository: GitHub – Used for storing project files, managing code versions, and collaborating among team members.
  • Web Application Framework: Stream lit – Used to develop an interactive web application and display soil information, crop recommendations, and analytical results.
  • Data Management & Analysis: Microsoft Excel (Spreadsheet) – Used for organizing soil data, nutrient information, crop details, fertilizer recommendations, and maintaining datasets.

Creativity and Innovation

Field Shift combines farm location, soil-test information, previous crop history and historical climate data into a single web-based platform. Instead of selecting crops randomly, farmers can use collected agricultural information to support more informed crop selection and crop rotation planning.USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) IN THE PROJECTAI-assisted tools can support application development, Python code preparation, debugging and documentation. The main crop-screening process uses farm details, soil information and NASA POWER climate data. The actual recommendation process depends on the logic implemented in the application.
